content:
Let me analyze the teaching examples more carefully to identify the correction rules.

Looking at Example 1 (2023-12-20):
- History: Prices declining from 76.46 → 66.73 (last 18 days)
- Model forecast: Starts at 75.29, ends at 71.80 after 30 days
- True outcomes: Starts at 75.36, ends at 62.41 after 30 days

The model is significantly too high, especially after day 10+. The true prices have dropped more than expected.

Looking at Example 2 (2024-06-26):
- History: Prices around 67.23 → 69.96
- Model forecast: Starts at 67.32, ends at 70.55 after 30 days
- True outcomes: Starts at 67.23, ends at 69.96

Wait, looking more carefully at Example 2:
- Day 1: Model 67.32 vs True 67.23 (error: +0.09)
- Day 5: Model 71.71 vs True 70.93 (error: +0.78)
- Day 10: Model 69.91 vs True 67.96 (error: +1.95)
- Day 15: Model 67.96 vs True 66.42 (error: +1.54)
- Day 18: Model 67.80 vs True 66.00 (error: +1.80)
- Day 25: Model 70.52 vs True 68.58 (error: +1.94)
- Day 30: Model 70.53 vs True 68.86 (error: +1.67)

The model consistently overestimates prices, especially as we go further into the future. The error seems to increase with horizon.

Looking at Example 3 (2023-12-21):
This is essentially the same as Example 1 but with different history (last price on day 18 is 75.36 instead of 71.93).


- Day 1: Model 78.17 vs True 78.14 (close)
- Day 5: Model 80.80 vs True 80.24 (error: +0.56)
- Day 10: Model 73.63 vs True 72.05 (error: +1.58)
- Day 15: Model 71.56 vs True 66.
